label: digit 3 as an original-phase input
explanation: Token detector for the digit 3 while the original sequence is being read. It fires on every original-phase step whose input is 3 (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.9999). It is silent on all other tokens, including the other digits 0-2, and silent on the <DEL> step. It almost never fires when 3 shows up as a fed-back input during the copy phase (16 activations on dev). Magnitude is highest when 3 comes early in the sequence (t=0 activations reach about 2.84) and falls with position: by t=7-8 activations are around 0.3-0.4 of max, and mean mass per activation at t=8 is about a third of that at t=0. Repeat occurrences of 3 in the same sequence (in_first=0) fire more weakly than first occurrences. Sequences that start with 3 or contain more digits have more firing steps only because they contain 3s more often.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split the predicate has 0 false positives and 12 misses. All 12 misses are near-zero activations (0.00 to 0.03 of max, 0.0% of activation mass) at step L+1, when a fed-back 3 enters during the copy phase right after a sequence that started with 3. This is negligible residue, not a separate behaviour.
The test score is F1 0.99994 with recall 0.99989, not exactly 1.000 as reported. The difference is trivial.

Checked factual claims against the dev profile. The <DEL> step has 0 activations. The copy phase has 16 activations, matching the claim. Tokens other than 3, including digits 0-2, have 0 activations. Max activation is 2.839, reached at t=0. Mean mass per activation is 1.16e-5 at t=0 and 3.6e-6 at t=8, a ratio of about 0.31, so 'about a third' holds. Low-quartile examples at t=7-8 sit at 0.30-0.38 of max, as claimed.

The claim that repeat occurrences fire more weakly is weakly supported but confounded with position. Mean mass per activation is about 7.3e-6 when in_first=0 versus 9.4e-6 when in_first=1, and repeats necessarily come later in the sequence. This is a minor descriptive point.
The higher rates for first_tok=3 and for sequences with many digits come from those sequences containing more 3s; this is consistent with the orig_idx rate being flat at 0.034 across every position.
